evidence.title: About local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot
evidence.locator: Local sandboxing; How it works; Configuring; Cross-platform support; Enterprise policy enforcement
evidence.finding: Local sandboxing (CLI and app) is off by default and is lightweight OS process/filesystem containment via MXC, not a VM or container. It restricts filesystem paths, outbound and local network or per-host rules, and credentials: sandboxed tools get placeholders and a local proxy supplies real credentials only to approved HTTPS hosts. Built-in CLI file tools run in-process outside the OS sandbox and honour policy best-effort. The app can change sandboxing for an active local session. Managed settings can require sandboxing and fail closed when unavailable; /sandbox disable turns it off where policy permits bypass.

evidence.locator: Types of memories; Where available; Storage and ownership; How memories are created; Reinforced and retired; Retention and expiry
evidence.finding: Copilot Memory stores repository facts (shared with read-access collaborators, per repository, not pooled, not copied to forks) and user preferences, used across the app, CLI, code review, cloud agent, Mobile, Slack and Teams. Facts cite code and preferences cite the user's words; Copilot checks citations against the current branch and upvotes or downvotes memories. Memories cannot be created or edited directly on GitHub.com; CLI imports memories in bulk. Write-access users delete facts, users delete preferences, and Business/Enterprise admins can export or delete preferences. Default expiry is 90 days; owners can set 7-180 days for repository facts.

evidence.finding: GitHub applies temporary rate limits for capacity and fairness; users are told to wait and retry, check usage or upgrade.

evidence.title: Configure the development environment for agents on GitHub Actions
evidence.locator: Copilot setup steps; Preinstalling tools; Self-hosted runners
evidence.finding: copilot-setup-steps.yml preinstalls tools for Actions-based sessions; the example caches npm dependencies; only settings such as steps, services and timeout-minutes (maximum 59) are honoured. Secrets and variables for cloud agent are configured separately. Actions sessions can run on ephemeral self-hosted runners via ARC with the integrated firewall disabled.

evidence.title: Getting started with the GitHub Copilot app
evidence.locator: Prerequisites; Opening the app; Connecting a repository or folder; First code changes; Orienting yourself
evidence.finding: Prerequisites are a GitHub account, a Copilot plan or own model provider credentials, and Git. Onboarding signs in to GitHub (GHE.com hostnames supported; GHES accounts added later), offers a plan or a model provider, then connects repositories or local folders, including clones from other Git hosts. A session is started with a mode and prompt; Changes shows the diff and Create PR opens a pull request. Customize discovers and manages plugins, skills, MCP servers and canvases.

evidence.title: Using Copilot cloud agent on GitHub Mobile
evidence.locator: Starting a session; Assigning an issue to Copilot; Tracking sessions
evidence.finding: On Mobile an issue is assigned to Copilot through its Assignees; sessions can be started from issues, PRs or repositories, and the session list can be searched and filtered, for example Open or Merged.

evidence.title: Third-party coding agents
evidence.locator: Introduction; Where you can use coding agents; Making coding agents available; Partner agents
evidence.finding: Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex coding agents are public preview, run alongside Copilot, are started from the Agents tab, issues, PR mentions, Mobile or VS Code, and must be enabled by user, organization or enterprise policy. Enabling them installs a GitHub App for each agent and they can be powered by the existing Copilot subscription. They open PRs, request review and iterate on PR comments; they are separate agent sessions.

evidence.title: Using Copilot cloud agent via the API
evidence.locator: Agent tasks API; Authentication; Starting, listing, status; Issues API
evidence.finding: Agent tasks API (public preview) creates, lists and gets tasks by ID; states are queued, in_progress, completed, failed, idle, waiting_for_user, timed_out and cancelled. It accepts only user-to-server tokens (PAT, OAuth app, GitHub App user token); installation tokens are unsupported. REST and GraphQL issue APIs (public preview) assign GitHub issues to Copilot with target repo, base branch, instructions, custom agent and model.

evidence.title: Supported AI models in GitHub Copilot
evidence.locator: Supported AI models; Model retirement history
evidence.finding: Generally available models come from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Moonshot AI and xAI. The retirement table lists models retired on 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-16 with suggested alternatives.

evidence.title: Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot
evidence.locator: Pricing tables; Copilot code review cost considerations
evidence.finding: Model prices are per 1M tokens, for example Claude Sonnet 5.5 $2.00 input and $10.00 output. Copilot code review uses an undisclosed model and publishes only estimated typical credit ranges per review effort level.

evidence.title: Accessing compliance reports for your enterprise
evidence.finding: Enterprise settings provide downloadable SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, CSA CAIQ, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, CSA STAR and other reports from the Compliance page. The page does not state report periods or name Copilot scope.

evidence.title: Adding sub-issues
evidence.locator: Overview; Creating; Adding existing issues; GitHub CLI
evidence.finding: Issues take up to 100 sub-issues per parent and eight nesting levels; existing issues, including from other repositories, can be added; projects can group and filter by parent. gh issue create --parent and gh issue edit --add-sub-issue manage them.

evidence.title: Creating issue dependencies
evidence.locator: Marking blocked by or blocking; GitHub CLI
evidence.finding: Issues can be marked blocked by or blocking others; blocked issues show a Blocked icon on project boards and Issues pages; gh issue create/edit/view manage and read dependencies by issue number or URL.

evidence.title: About GitHub Support
evidence.finding: Paid plans, Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise contact GitHub Support directly; GitHub Free users use Community discussions except for account, security and abuse. Preview features and Copilot output correctness are out of support scope.

evidence.title: The latest GitHub and GitHub Copilot SOC reports are now available
evidence.finding: SOC 1, 2 and 3 reports covering Copilot Business and Enterprise apply to 2024-04-01 to 2024-09-30 and are available on the GitHub Enterprise Trust Center; Copilot gained Type II coverage after earlier Type I reports.

evidence.title: Remote control for Copilot CLI sessions now generally available
evidence.finding: Remote control streams a CLI session in real time to Mobile and github.com, supports non-GitHub repositories and directories without a repository, and lets users steer, review plans, stop the session, approve or deny permission requests and answer questions. Business and Enterprise need remote control and CLI policies enabled.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot app generally available
evidence.finding: The app is GA on macOS, Windows and Linux; canvases are bidirectional surfaces where the user and agent operate on the same plan, pull request, terminal or browser session.

evidence.title: Copilot automations
evidence.locator: Overview; Availability and permissions; Personal and shared automations; Triggers; Billing; Proposed improvements; Security and safety
evidence.finding: Automations run cloud agent on schedules, repository events or the API; they are managed from the Agents tab, the app, VS Code and the REST API. Write access is needed to create them. Shared automations act as Copilot, belong to the repository and keep working if the creator leaves; personal ones act as the creator, who cannot approve their PRs. Runs are visible to everyone with read access, including prompt, logs and changes. AI-credit limits: per run (minimum 30) stops a run; daily, weekly and monthly limits stop new runs but not running ones. Automations can propose changes to their own tools, triggers and prompts.

evidence.title: Set AI credit session limits in Copilot CLI and SDK
evidence.finding: CLI and SDK session limits (public preview) track AI credits across a session; /limits views or sets them and --max-ai-credits bounds a run. They are a soft cap that may be slightly exceeded and complement budgets.

evidence.title: GitHub Mobile: Live notifications for Copilot CLI sessions
evidence.finding: GitHub Mobile live notifications cover cloud coding agent sessions and remote CLI sessions, with states In progress, Waiting for user input, Idle and Finished.

evidence.title: Upcoming changes to GitHub Copilot policies and billing
evidence.finding: For card or PayPal customers, new Business and Enterprise seat assignments are paid upfront; revoking a seat gives no prorated refund. Unified Copilot on github.com retains chat data for the life of the account instead of 28 days.

evidence.title: Client telemetry user attribution and configurable capture
evidence.finding: In CLI, the app and VS Code Agent Host, OpenTelemetry identity capture (user.name, process.user.name, host.name) is off by default and separate from an existing pseudonymous identifier; prompt, response, tool argument, tool output and policy detail capture classes are each off by default and managed values take precedence.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot supports server-to-server authentication
evidence.finding: In public preview, SDK services can use GitHub App installation tokens with the Copilot Requests organization permission; usage is billed to the organization, appears in AI usage CSV reports with app_client_id, and owners stop access by suspending or uninstalling the app.

evidence.title: Agent Merge watches and fixes pull requests in the cloud
evidence.finding: Agent Merge watches a PR and fixes failing Actions workflows, merge conflicts or both in a cloud environment, and can be combined with auto-merge; paid plans.

evidence.title: Copilot code review: Merge with confidence with Max and approvals
evidence.finding: Max effort (public preview) runs several independent review agents across providers plus an aggregation agent. Reviews include an approval assessment in the overview comment; approvals (GA, off by default) count toward required approvals and are dismissed when new commits are pushed. Admins set default and maximum effort and which paths Copilot may approve.

evidence.title: github/gh-aw repository
evidence.finding: GitHub Agentic Workflows repository is MIT licensed per repository metadata; latest prerelease v1.3.1 published 2026-11-18.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot app, Universe releases
evidence.finding: App projects (public preview) hold repositories, design mocks, Slack threads and notes; Copilot coordinates agents in the background and checks in when it needs the user; focused single-repository sessions remain. Slack and Figma context and image generation are available.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot SDK is becoming Microsoft Copilot SDK
evidence.finding: GitHub Copilot SDK is moving in phases to the Microsoft organization as Microsoft Copilot SDK; support stays the same.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile
evidence.locator: Comparison of Actions-based sessions and cloud sandboxes; Access and availability; Ways to work; Session history; Customize; Limitations
evidence.finding: Chat data is retained 28 days for Actions-based sessions and for the life of the account for cloud sandbox sessions. Without write access a session is read-only. Agentic work runs tests and linters; code review comments and suggests fixes. Hooks run commands during agent work; custom instructions (personal, repository, organization), custom agents and agent skills apply. Session logs show work and tools. Remote control keeps a CLI session on the local machine, which must stay online. Actions sessions support self-hosted runners and have a 59-minute limit. Copilot only works with GitHub-hosted repositories; new cloud experience requires a paid plan.

evidence.title: Issue artifacts are now in public preview
evidence.finding: Issue artifacts (public preview) attach Markdown, HTML and link artifacts to issues; app sessions attach artifacts automatically; gh issue artifact creates, edits, lists, views, downloads and deletes them, with image and video attachments; artifacts are edited on github.com with version history.

evidence.title: New tools, triggers, and cost controls for Copilot Automations
evidence.finding: Automations gain API triggers, issue triggers including closed, reopened and status changed, PR triggers, chaining, and tools to upload image or video attachments, merge PRs, mark PRs ready or draft and update comments; per-run, daily, weekly and monthly credit limits.

evidence.title: Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion
evidence.finding: Copilot Fusion routes and orchestrates models per prompt (single, cascade, critique). GitHub reports a Fusion Max score of 60 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index without fixture or attempt detail.

evidence.title: Work from anywhere with a new, connected Copilot cloud experience
evidence.finding: One session continues across web, Mobile, app, VS Code and CLI with the same session list; sandboxes snapshot and resume. Mobile accepts voice and image input; Slack and Teams @GitHub create issues and sessions. Built-in connectors (Sentry, Linear, Cloudflare), key-auth MCP and skills apply. Chat sessions are scoped to one organization or personal repositories by default; enterprise agent permission and MCP allowlist settings apply. Paid plans only; Free keeps Copilot Chat.

evidence.title: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is generally available and more
evidence.finding: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is GA; it creates issues, implements changes and opens PRs. Canvas in Teams shows plans, code changes and previews beside the discussion. Created issues and PRs say "Created from a Slack/Teams conversation with @username".

evidence.title: GitHub Changelog: Copilot label
evidence.finding: Lists November 2026 Copilot entries, including models deprecated on 2026-11-16 and upcoming December model deprecations announced 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-17.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot plans
evidence.finding: Business and Enterprise list per-user monthly prices and pooled usage: included AI credits are shared organization-wide with admin spending controls.

evidence.title: github/app README
evidence.locator: README at 6e4ad0f; repository contents; latest release v1.4.3 (2026-11-19)
evidence.finding: The public repo hosts releases, issues, discussions and changelog only (License: all rights reserved; contents .github, docs, flags, changelog, README). Any Copilot plan including Free works, or BYOK without a plan. Canvases show plans, terminals, browser previews, diffs and workflow state; My Work gathers sessions, issues and PRs.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot app v1.2.0
evidence.finding: v1.2.0 adds an Open in menu with a GitHub Mobile QR code to continue cloud and Codespace sessions, GitHub Enterprise Server accounts in Settings > Accounts, and filtering issues and PRs by custom fields such as a Project Size.

evidence.title: github/copilot-cli repository
evidence.finding: The repository contains README, changelog, install script, container files and a proprietary GitHub Copilot CLI License (run and redistribute unmodified copies), not CLI source. Latest stable release v1.0.114 (2026-11-18); prerelease v1.0.115-5 (2026-11-21).

evidence.title: Agent management
evidence.finding: The Agents tab and Copilot home start sessions with Copilot, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI Codex or custom agents, show live session logs in real time, list active sessions, accept steering input mid-session, open a session in VS Code or Copilot CLI, and link to the resulting pull request for review and merge.

evidence.title: microsoft/copilot-sdk repository
evidence.locator: README: overview, FAQ (subscription, billing, BYOK), status line 154; Releases
evidence.finding: github/copilot-sdk now redirects to microsoft/copilot-sdk (MIT). The README calls it Microsoft Copilot SDK for Python, TypeScript, Go, .NET, Java and Rust, exposing the Copilot CLI engine, and says it is generally available and follows semantic versioning. Its FAQ says a Copilot subscription is required unless BYOK keys are used, and SDK prompts are billed like Copilot CLI usage. Latest stable release v2.0.1 (2026-11-18, tag commit 3ce6145); the GitHub API marks v2.0.2-preview.4 (2026-11-21) as a prerelease.

evidence.title: microsoft/vscode extensions/copilot
evidence.locator: Directory listing at bfbf12b; archived microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat README
evidence.finding: microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat (MIT) is archived and says the extension moved into microsoft/vscode; extensions/copilot at commit bfbf12b holds its source (src, package.json, LICENSE.txt).

evidence.title: GitHub Status incidents API
evidence.finding: Status has Copilot and Copilot AI Model Providers components; recent incidents include critical 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-11 and major 2026-11-09 Copilot incidents.

evidence.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
evidence.locator: Where you can use MCP; Default MCP servers; Personal MCP servers; Repository-level configuration; Best practices
evidence.finding: Cloud agent starts with the GitHub MCP server (read-only token scoped to the current repository by default) and Playwright (reads pages and takes screenshots on localhost). Connectors are GitHub-verified servers whose authentication GitHub handles. Personal MCP servers support key-based auth via COPILOT_MCP_ secrets and are only for the user. Repository administrators configure repository servers for everyone with write access; remote OAuth servers are unsupported there. The tools field allowlists tools; delegated work calls configured MCP tools without approval. The app discovers and installs MCP servers from Customize.

evidence.title: Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent
evidence.locator: Unvalidated code; Push changes; Sensitive information; Prompt injection; Auditability; Automations
evidence.finding: Only write-access users trigger the agent and only their comments reach it. It pushes to one copilot/ branch or the PR branch it was asked on, subject to branch protection and required checks; it cannot mark PRs ready, approve or merge. Workflows wait for a write-access user to Approve and run. The requester cannot approve the PR; unattributed PRs need an extra approval. Internet access is firewalled. CodeQL, advisory and secret-scanning validation results and actions appear in the session log, and Copilot code review gives a second opinion. Commits are authored by Copilot with the requester as co-author, signed and Verified, and link to session logs; session logs and audit log events are available to administrators. Shared automations act as Copilot.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot CLI
evidence.locator: Modes of use; Steering; Automatic context management; Customizing; Trusted directories; Allowed tools; Model usage; Using your own model provider
evidence.finding: Interactive mode with plan mode; manual approval offers allow once, allow for the session (restored on resume) or reject with feedback. --allow-tool, --allow-all-tools and --deny-tool take shell(COMMAND), write and MCP tool specifications; deny takes precedence. /permissions assisted lets a model approve requests it judges safe. Trusted-directory scoping is heuristic. Auto-compaction runs at about 95% of the token limit; /context shows token usage. Custom instructions, custom agents, hooks, skills and Copilot Memory are supported; reasoning levels are configurable. BYOK connects OpenAI-compatible, Azure OpenAI or Anthropic endpoints, including local Ollama and vLLM.

evidence.title: Custom agents
evidence.locator: About agent profiles; Where you can use custom agents
evidence.finding: Agent profiles are Markdown files with instructions that can restrict available tools and configure MCP servers; they are shared at repository, organization and enterprise level and used in the app, CLI, cloud agent and supported IDEs.

evidence.title: Data available in Copilot usage metrics
evidence.locator: User and enterprise report fields; Customization fields
evidence.finding: Usage metrics API reports distinct and top custom agents, skills and MCP servers used per user and per enterprise or organization.

evidence.title: Managing GitHub Copilot in the cloud for your enterprise or organization
evidence.locator: Managing the Copilot in the cloud policy; firewall; third-party agents
evidence.finding: Enterprise owners set the Copilot in the cloud policy for all or selected organizations and enable third-party agents; organization owners block the cloud agent in repositories, configure the agent firewall and choose which enabled agents to allow. The page no longer names an AI manager role.

evidence.title: Abilities of roles in an enterprise
evidence.locator: About roles in an enterprise (table); Enterprise owners
evidence.finding: Predefined enterprise roles with stated permissions: enterprise owner (all settings, members and policies, including enforcing policy across organizations), billing manager, enterprise open-source license manager, app manager, security manager (public preview), user and guest collaborator, plus custom roles. No AI manager role is listed.

evidence.title: GitHub Docs: Authenticating Copilot CLI
evidence.locator: 'Using Copilot CLI without GitHub authentication' > 'Offline mode'
evidence.finding: With COPILOT_OFFLINE=true, 'First-party client-side telemetry is disabled'; 'Without offline mode, even when using BYOK without GitHub authentication, telemetry is still sent normally.'
